column2: req_desc

Comparison operators
Filters support the equality, inequality, range and set operators with the type-class rules and worked results given in Business rules.

Logical operators
Filters combine conditions with `$and`, `$or`, `$nor` and `$not` as worked in Business rules, and any other operator is refused with `unknown_operator`.

Array matching
Dot paths, array positions, whole-array and any-element matching, `$size` and `$elemMatch` give the results worked in Business rules.

Missing and null fields
`$exists`, null equality and `$ne: null` treat missing fields exactly as Business rules states.

Document rules
Inserts, edits and loads enforce the `_id` format, allowed values, field names, the size limit and the depth limit, refusing each with its API error.

Query status announcement
After every run the Query status live region carries the exact match text from Feedback states.

Results grid keyboard
The Table view is a grid with one tabbable cell, where the arrow keys, Home and End move focus and Enter opens that row's document.

Array filter journey
A builder runs an array filter with Ctrl+Enter on a seeded collection, reads the announced count and the matched rows, and opens a matched document from the grid by keyboard.

Comparison order
Values of mixed types compare and sort in the single type order and within-type rules of Business rules.

Multi-key sort
Sorts take several keys in order, sort arrays by their smallest or largest element, and break ties by `_id` ascending.

Result pages
Query results are paged at `JARFUL_PAGE_SIZE` with `limit` capping the match count, and the pager moves by keyboard.

Phone workspace tabs
Below 768 CSS pixels the query bar, results and pipeline become the Query, Results and Pipeline tabs, moved with the arrow keys.

Mixed sort journey
A builder sorts a mixed-type collection by two keys, reads the row order, pages forward by keyboard, and sees the same order in the phone Results tab.

Projection rules
Projections include, exclude or drop `_id` as worked in Business rules, and a mix is refused with `invalid_projection`.

Number and date display
List, Table, JSON view, stage previews and schema show numbers and dates under the one display rule in Business rules.

View switch
The View radio group switches results between List, Table and JSON with the arrow keys, without running the query again.

Query error alerts
Refused queries show the exact Query error copy from Feedback states.

Projection views journey
A builder applies inclusion, exclusion and `_id`-free projections, gets the mixed-projection alert, and checks that the same number text appears in all three views.

Stage preview counts
The preview route returns exact counts and first documents for every stage prefix, honouring disabled stages and the stage limit.

Shaping stages
`$match`, `$project`, `$sort`, `$limit`, `$skip` and `$count` behave as worked in Business rules.

Unwind stage
`$unwind` emits one document per array element, drops missing, null and empty arrays, and passes non-arrays through unchanged.

Pipeline draft
Each person's working pipeline for a collection, including stage order and disabled stages, is kept on the server and survives reload, with the most recent save winning.

Keyboard stage editing
Stages are added, moved with Alt+Up and Alt+Down, disabled and deleted through the confirmation dialog by keyboard, with focus going back to the stage acted on.

Drag reorder
Dragging a stage by its move handle reorders it with the same result, announcement and persistence as the keyboard move.

Pipeline announcements
Every stage card shows its status text, and moves and recomputes are announced in the polite Pipeline status region with the copy from Feedback states.

Keyboard pipeline journey
A builder builds a match, unwind, group and sort pipeline by keyboard only, reads each stage's count, reorders a stage with Alt+Up, and deletes a stage through the dialog.

Group keys and order
`$group` accepts null, a path or an object of paths as its key and orders its output by key in the comparison order.

Accumulators
`$sum`, `$avg`, `$min`, `$max`, `$count`, `$push`, `$first` and `$last` compute the values worked in Business rules, including the `$avg` rounding.

Stage Sieve bars
Each enabled stage band draws a bar whose width follows the published log ratio to within 1 pixel, with an overflow notch above the input and a thin pass-through band for a disabled stage.

Stage Sieve motion
When stage k changes, bands k to n animate width and numeral from old to new with the published stagger and duration while earlier bands stay still.

Stage Sieve under reduced motion
With the reduced-motion setting on, bars, numerals and the pin marker take their final state in the first frame, and the announcements still happen.

Pinned document
Pinning a document by `_id` places a marker at the first stage that drops it, and that stage's label says so.

Grouping journey
A builder groups a seeded collection with every accumulator, checks the group order and rounded averages in the preview, and watches the Stage Sieve settle, mid-way with the clock and instantly under reduced motion.

Index management
Owners create single and compound indexes with default or given names, list them and drop them, and `_id_` is always present.

Unique index enforcement
A unique index refuses a second equal value on insert, edit and load with `duplicate_key`, and exactly one of two simultaneous equal inserts succeeds.

Unique index over existing data
Creating a unique index over existing duplicates is refused with the value of the first document, in `_id` order, whose key value already appeared earlier.

Index choice and examined counts
Every query plan picks an index or a full scan and counts the examined documents by the rules in Business rules.

Explain readout
The Query plan region shows and announces the plan's index or full scan and its examined and returned counts for the query that ran.

Duplicate notice in the editor
A save that hits a unique index shows the duplicate text naming the value and index in the editor's Save status.

Index and explain journey
An owner sees a full scan, creates a unique index from the Indexes form by keyboard, sees the index used, and an editor in another browser gets the duplicate notice on Ctrl+S.

Validator rules
Owners set a validator of required fields and per-path type, minimum, maximum and enum, which is checked on insert, edit and load but never against stored documents.

Validation check order
The first failing rule, in the published check order, is reported with its path and rule name.

Validation notice
A refused save shows the exact validation text from Feedback states as an icon chip in the editor and announces it politely.

Rules screen by role
Only owners can change rules on the Rules screen; editors and readers see the rules read-only with no save control.

Validation journey
An owner sets a rule, an editor in another browser is refused at the first failing path with the exact text, and the editor's fixed document then saves.

Schema summary values
The schema summary reads the first `JARFUL_SCHEMA_SAMPLE` documents and reports each path's presence and type shares as rounded whole percents.

Schema screen
The Schema screen lists every path with its presence text and proportional type segments that print their percentages.

Schema journey
A builder reads presence and type shares on a seeded collection, another person inserts a document, and reopening the Schema screen shows the changed shares, also on the phone layout.

Document versions
Every document has a server-kept version that starts at 1 and rises by 1 on each save, and a save with a stale version is refused with `version_conflict`.

Edit clash notice
A stale save shows the clash alert, where Reload loads the server copy and Overwrite saves the draft over it.

Editor keyboard
In the document editor Ctrl or Cmd+S saves, Tab indents, Escape then Tab leaves it, and closing the editor returns focus to the document that opened it.

Document deletion
Editors and owners delete a document through a confirmation dialog, and a later save of that document shows the deleted notice.

Edit clash journey
Two people open one document, the first saves with Ctrl+S, the second gets the clash alert, Reload shows the first person's text, and Overwrite then wins with the next version.

Change feed
Every insert, edit and delete in a collection is sent on that collection's event stream with its collection sequence number, which rises by 1 with no gaps.

Feed catch-up
A client that reconnects from its last sequence receives every missed change once, in order, with no duplicates or gaps.

Live results
An open results view shows other people's changes within 2 seconds, without a reload, moving focus or touching the editor draft, as qualified in Interactions.

Reader workspace
A reader sees the read-only note, a read-only editor and no insert, save, delete, load or rules controls.

Live collection journey
A reader with a filter active watches an editor's inserts, edits and deletes appear, change and leave, with the status count updating and no reload.

Sign-up with an emailed code
Sign-up emails a six-digit code, and the account works only after that code is entered.

Sign-in and sessions
People sign in with email and password, get an HTTP-only session cookie, land on the projects screen, and sign out from the Account menu.

Invitations
Owners invite an address as editor or reader, and an invitation moves only from pending to accepted or revoked, refusing every other move.

Invitation email
Each invitation sends one Mailpit message to the invited address with the published subject and the line naming the inviter, project and role.

Role checks per request
Every request checks the caller's current role, so readers cannot write and only owners manage members, indexes, rules, collections and the project.

Not found for outsiders
A project, collection, document, saved query, file or invitation the caller cannot open answers exactly like one that does not exist, in the API and on screen.

Downgrade in an open editor
After an owner downgrades an editor to reader, that person's next save is refused and their open editor becomes read-only within 2 seconds.

Landing routes
Creating a project lands on its first collection's address, accepting an invitation lands on the project's collection list, and reloading either address shows the same screen.

Members screen
Owners see members and pending invitations, change roles, remove members and revoke invitations on the Members screen.

Invitation journey
An owner invites an address, the invitee reads the email, signs up with the code and accepts, sees the read-only note as reader, gets Not found for another project, and saves after the owner raises their role.

File stored before parsing
A loaded file is parsed only after object storage confirms it holds the exact bytes, and a download is offered only after it is stored.

JSON lines loading
JSON-lines files load one document per non-blank line under the document and validation rules.

CSV loading
CSV files need a header row, follow standard CSV quoting, build nested fields from dotted headers and infer cell types as Business rules states.

All-or-nothing load report
A load with any bad line or too many lines adds nothing and reports up to 20 numbered line errors, and a clean load reports its exact count.

Original file download
Every stored upload can be downloaded byte for byte as uploaded, next to its load report.

Collection downloads
Downloads hold every document matching the current filter and sort, as JSON lines or as CSV with the published columns.

Spreadsheet-safe CSV
CSV download cells that start with a formula character get a leading apostrophe so a spreadsheet runs nothing.

File storage outage
When object storage is unreachable, file routes are refused and the banner shows, while browsing, editing and queries keep working.

File journey
A builder loads a file with known bad lines and sees the exact line list with nothing added, loads the fixed file and a CSV, downloads and reads back the data, and sees the outage banner on the storage-down instance.

Scan guard
A query, pipeline or download that would examine more than `JARFUL_SCAN_LIMIT` documents is refused with the guard message, and the Stage Sieve shows every count as at most the limit.

Bounded requests
Over-deep queries are refused, and every query, preview and download within the published limits answers within 3 seconds.

Saved queries
Editors and owners save named queries that survive reload and show their last run's server time and match count, and readers can run them.

Phone editor by touch
On a phone, tapping a document opens the editor full screen with Save and Close, and every action stays reachable by touch.

Closed panels are inert
A closed drawer, menu, dialog or hidden tab panel is hidden, cannot receive focus or pointer input, and is absent from the accessibility tree at every viewport.

Guard and phone journey
A builder hits the scan guard on a large collection, adds an index and runs it, saves the query and finds it with its count after reload, then edits and saves a document by touch on a phone.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest and answers the health route as Deployment states.

Grading seed route
The key-protected grading route creates confirmed users, projects, members, collections, documents, indexes, validators and saved queries in one call and returns their ids.

Projects and collections
Owners create and delete projects and collections, and every screen agrees with the stored document counts, also after reload.

Error shape and order
Every API error uses the one published body shape, and the first applicable error in the published order wins.

Server boundary
The server is same-origin only, enforces body-size and content-type limits, never serves source or credentials, and keeps starting when a dependency is down.

Configuration from the environment
Every service address, credential and limit is read from the published environment variables at start and never hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Published breakpoints
The workspace shows rail, list and editor side by side from 1280 CSS pixels, rail with stacked panes from 768, and the phone layout below 768.

Resizable panes
The query and pipeline pane separators resize by pointer and by arrow keys in steps of 5 percent and report their value.

Dialog keyboard handling
Every open dialog and drawer keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside it, closes on Escape and returns focus to its opener.

Landing hero sample
The landing page's hero card runs the published sample pipeline over the built-in houseplant collection with exact server counts in the Stage Sieve.

Empty, loading and not-found screens
Empty collections, loading panes and unreachable pages show the published headline, a layout-holding skeleton and the Not found heading.

Pink field look
Every screen sits on the bubblegum pink field with TikTok Sans display and body type, a single lime primary action and the published corner rule.

Working screens look
Lists, tables, editors, previews, chips, banners and schema bars follow the working-screen language in Visual design.

Hero look
The landing hero shows the stretched JARFUL wordmark with its lime swipe beside the black glowing Stage Sieve card, with text first on a phone.
`/app/run.json` exists with string `install`, `build` and `serve` and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`, and nothing else is needed to start the app.
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at `/app` lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`) and every bundled font, each with its licence.
Every shipped package and bundled font uses one of MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0 or OFL-1.1.
Data lives only in PostgreSQL and MinIO: no SQLite, no file-based database, no extra cache or queue service.
The provided service configuration and dev credentials stay as provided.
The browser loads nothing from another origin: fonts, icons, scripts and styles are bundled.
Application source is TypeScript, and the npm lockfile is committed.
